blocks.text: Asosiy qoida qizil kitobdan tanish (→ qizil kitob, 72-dars): biror tur haqida **umuman** gapirganda artikl qo'yilmaydi — sanaladigan ot ko'plikda (**Children** love games), sanalmaydigan ot o'z holicha (**Music** helps me relax). Aniq narsa yoki guruh haqida esa — **the** (**the children** in my class, **the music** at the party). O'zbekchada ikkala holatda ham «bolalar», «musiqa» — hech qanday belgi yo'q. Bu darsda B1–B2 darajadagi qiyin joylarni ko'ramiz: sifat va who-gap qo'shilganda nima bo'ladi, mavhum ot qachon **the ... of** oladi, va **most people** bilan **most of the people** farqi.

rows: **The children** are playing in the garden. (bizning bolalar)
**The crime** shocked the whole town. (o'sha jinoyat)
**Tourists** often get lost in the old city.
**The tourists** on our bus were from Japan.
**The water** in this lake is very cold.
**The smartphones** in this shop are cheap.

blocks.text: Ko'p o'quvchilar «otga sifat yoki who-gap qo'shilsa, u aniq bo'ladi — demak **the**» deb o'ylaydi. Bu xato. **Young people**, **Italian food**, **modern art**, **people who smoke**, **cars made in Korea** — bularning hammasi hamon **umumiy toifa**: dunyodagi har qanday yosh, har qanday chekadigan odam. Sifat toifani toraytiradi, lekin uni yopiq guruhga aylantirmaydi. **the** faqat guruh **chegaralangan va aniq** bo'lganda keladi: **the young people** in our street (ko'chamizdagi aniq yoshlar), **the people who** live next door (qo'shnilarimiz).

rows: **The young people** in our street organised a clean-up.
**The people who** live next door smoke on the balcony.
**The food** at the wedding was delicious.
**Cars made in Korea** are popular here.
**The cars** in the car park belong to the staff.

items.text: **The young drivers** in our company had a safety course.
**People who** live near the sea live longer, some studies say.
items.translation: Ba'zi tadqiqotlarga ko'ra, dengiz yaqinida yashaydigan **odamlar** uzoqroq umr ko'radi.

blocks.text: Mavhum otlar: history — the history of ...

Mavhum otlar (life, history, education, crime, society, technology, art, law) umumiy ma'noda artiklsiz: **History** was my favourite subject. Lekin **of** bilan aniqlansa — **the**: **the history of** Bukhara, **the life of** Navoi, **the role of** parents. Qiziq tomoni: ma'no bir xil bo'lsa ham, sifat bilan — artiklsiz, **of** bilan — **the**: **Uzbek history** = **the history of** Uzbekistan. Shuning uchun artiklni ma'noga emas, **tuzilishga** qarab tanlang.

items.text: I'm reading a book about **the history of** Bukhara.
**History** was my favourite subject at school.
**The role of** parents is very important.

blocks.text: most people — most of the people

Miqdor so'zlarida ham xuddi shu tanlov bor. Umumiy ma'noda — **most / all / some** + ot, artiklsiz: **Most people** check their phones before breakfast (dunyodagi ko'pchilik). Aniq guruh ichida — **most of the / all (of) the / some of the**: **Most of the people** I work with live outside the city. O'zbekchada farq qaratqich bilan ko'rinadi: «**ko'pchilik odamlar**» — «men bilan ishlaydigan **odamlarning ko'pchiligi**». «most of people» deyilmaydi: **of** bo'lsa — **the** (yoki my, these) ham bo'lishi shart. Batafsil — 88-dars.

items.text: **Most people** check their phones before breakfast.
**Most of the people** I work with live outside the city.
items.translation: Men bilan ishlaydigan **odamlarning ko'pchiligi** shahar tashqarisida yashaydi.

items.text: **All the children** in the class passed the exam.

blocks.text: Eng yaxshi mashq — bitta otni bir gapda ikki ma'noda ishlatish: I rarely drink **coffee**, but **the coffee** Kate made was wonderful. Birinchi qismda — umuman qahva, ikkinchisida — aniq bir piyola. Bunday gaplarda o'zbekcha tarjima ko'pincha egalik qo'shimchasi yoki aniqlovchi bilan farqni ko'rsatadi: «**qahva**» — «Keyt damlagan **qahva**».

O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «The young people today don't read» (umuman) → **Young people** today don't read; «The modern art is strange» → **Modern art** is strange; «History of Uzbekistan is long» → **The history of Uzbekistan** is long; «I study the international law» → **international law**; «Most of people» → **Most people** yoki **most of the people** (in my group); «The crime is rising» (umuman) → **Crime** is rising; «The people who smoke harm their health» (umuman) → **People who** smoke harm their health.

Ikki savol bering. 1) Gap bu turdagi **hamma** narsa yoki odam haqidami (dunyodagi barcha o'smirlar, har qanday zamonaviy san'at)? → artiklsiz, sifat va who-gap bo'lsa ham. 2) Gap **chegaralangan, ko'rsatib bo'ladigan guruh** haqidami (ko'chamizdagi yoshlar, kechagi ko'rgazmadagi rasmlar)? → **the**. Mavhum otdan keyin **of** kelsa — deyarli doim **the**.
Bog'liq darslar: a / an va the — 72-dars; the + birlik ot tur ma'nosida (the giraffe, the computer) va the + sifat (the rich, the elderly) — 76-dars; all / most / some (of) — 88-dars.

rows: **the children** in my class, **the people** next door
**most people** — **most of the** people at the meeting

examples.title: General plural: **Teenagers** need sleep, **cats** ...
examples.description: Biror tur haqida umuman gapirganda sanaladigan ot ko'plikda, artiklsiz. O'zbekchada ko'pincha birlik ishlatiladi: «O'smir ko'p uxlaydi», inglizchada — Teenagers sleep a lot.

sentences.text: **Teenagers** need more sleep than adults, according to doctors.
sentences.translation: Shifokorlarning aytishicha, **o'smirlarga** kattalarga qaraganda ko'proq uyqu kerak.

sentences.text: **Cats** are more independent than **dogs**, so they suit busy people.
sentences.translation: **Mushuklar** **itlarga** qaraganda mustaqilroq, shuning uchun band odamlarga mos keladi.

sentences.text: I'm not very good with **computers**, so my son sets everything up for me.
sentences.translation: **Kompyuterni** unchalik tushunmayman, shuning uchun hamma narsani o'g'lim sozlab beradi.

sentences.text: Do **bees** really die after they sting someone?
sentences.translation: **Asalarilar** rostdan ham chaqqandan keyin o'ladimi?

sentences.text: **Electric cars** are getting cheaper, but they're still expensive in Uzbekistan.
sentences.translation: **Elektromobillar** arzonlashib boryapti, lekin O'zbekistonda hali ham qimmat.

sentences.text: Madina has always been afraid of **spiders**, even tiny ones.
sentences.translation: Madina doim **o'rgimchakdan** qo'rqadi, hatto mittilaridan ham.

sentences.text: **Nurses** in the UK often work twelve-hour shifts.
sentences.translation: Buyuk Britaniyada **hamshiralar** ko'pincha o'n ikki soatlik smenada ishlaydi.

sentences.text: Why do **people** always complain about the weather?
sentences.translation: Nega **odamlar** doim ob-havodan shikoyat qiladi?

sentences.text: My grandfather says that **mobile phones** have made **children** lazy.
sentences.translation: Bobomning aytishicha, **mobil telefonlar** **bolalarni** dangasa qilib qo'ygan.

sentences.text: Although **tigers** are dangerous animals, they rarely attack **humans** unless they're very hungry.
sentences.translation: **Yo'lbarslar** xavfli hayvon bo'lsa ham, juda och qolmasa, **odamlarga** kamdan-kam hujum qiladi.

examples.title: General uncountable: **crime**, **technology**, **life**
examples.description: Sanalmaydigan va mavhum otlar umumiy ma'noda artiklsiz: life, crime, technology, education, health, unemployment, politics, art, money.

sentences.text: **Crime** has fallen in the city since they installed more cameras.
sentences.translation: Ko'proq kamera o'rnatilgandan beri shaharda **jinoyatchilik** kamaydi.

sentences.text: **Technology** is changing faster than schools can teach it.
sentences.translation: **Texnologiya** maktablar o'rgatishga ulgurolmaydigan darajada tez o'zgaryapti.

sentences.text: For many families, **education** is the most important investment.
sentences.translation: Ko'p oilalar uchun **ta'lim** eng muhim sarmoya.

sentences.text: **Life** in a big city can be lonely, even with millions of people around you.
sentences.translation: Katta shahardagi **hayot**, atrofda millionlab odam bo'lsa ham, yolg'izlikka to'la bo'lishi mumkin.

sentences.text: I'm not interested in **politics**, but I always vote.
sentences.translation: **Siyosatga** qiziqmayman, lekin doim ovoz beraman.

sentences.text: **Unemployment** among young people is a problem in many countries.
sentences.translation: Ko'p mamlakatlarda yoshlar orasida **ishsizlik** muammo bo'lib qolmoqda.

sentences.text: Nilufar studied **art** in Florence and now designs jewellery.
sentences.translation: Nilufar Florensiyada **san'at** bo'yicha o'qigan, hozir taqinchoqlar dizaynini yaratadi.

sentences.text: Is **money** more important to you than **free time**?
sentences.translation: Siz uchun **pul** **bo'sh vaqtdan** muhimroqmi?

sentences.text: **Air pollution** causes thousands of early deaths every year.
sentences.translation: **Havo ifloslanishi** har yili minglab bevaqt o'limlarga sabab bo'ladi.

sentences.text: **Health** is more important than **success**, but most of us only realise this when we get ill.
sentences.translation: **Sog'liq** **muvaffaqiyatdan** muhimroq, lekin ko'pchiligimiz buni faqat kasal bo'lganimizda tushunamiz.

examples.title: General or specific: **children** / **the children**
examples.description: Bitta otning ikki ma'nosi: umumiy (artiklsiz) va aniq guruh yoki narsa (the) — vaziyat yoki aniqlovchi qaysi biri ekanini ko'rsatadi.

sentences.text: **Children** usually love the zoo, but **the children** in my group were bored.
sentences.translation: **Bolalar** odatda hayvonot bog'ini yaxshi ko'radi, lekin mening guruhimdagi **bolalar** zerikib qolishdi.

sentences.text: Where are **the children**? — They're in the garden with their grandfather.
sentences.translation: **Bolalar** qani? — Bog'da, bobosi bilan.

sentences.text: **The traffic** this morning was so bad that I was an hour late.
sentences.translation: Bugun ertalab **tirbandlik** shunchalik dahshatli ediki, bir soat kechikdim.

sentences.text: I listen to **music** all day, but **the music** in that café drives me crazy.
sentences.translation: Kun bo'yi **musiqa** tinglayman, lekin o'sha kafedagi **musiqa** meni jinni qiladi.

sentences.text: **Doctors** earn a lot in the USA, but **the doctors** at our clinic are underpaid.
sentences.translation: AQShda **shifokorlar** ko'p maosh oladi, lekin bizning klinikadagi **shifokorlarga** kam haq to'lanadi.

sentences.text: Is **the tea** still hot, or shall I make some more?
sentences.translation: **Choy** hali issiqmi yoki yana damlab beraymi?

sentences.text: **Hotels** in Samarkand are full in spring, so book early.
sentences.translation: Bahorda Samarqanddagi **mehmonxonalar** to'lib ketadi, shuning uchun oldindan band qiling.

sentences.text: **The hotel** we stayed in had a wonderful view of the old city walls.
sentences.translation: Biz turgan **mehmonxonadan** eski shahar devorlarining ajoyib manzarasi ochilardi.

sentences.text: **Exams** make me nervous, but **the exam** yesterday was surprisingly easy.
sentences.translation: **Imtihonlar** meni hayajonga soladi, lekin kechagi **imtihon** kutilmaganda oson bo'ldi.

sentences.text: **Patience** is important when you teach, and **the patience** our teacher showed with Jasur was amazing.
sentences.translation: Dars berishda **sabr** muhim, o'qituvchimizning Jasurga ko'rsatgan **sabri** esa hayratlanarli edi.

examples.title: Adjectives don't change it: **young people**, **Italian food**
examples.description: Sifat qo'shilsa ham toifa umumiy bo'lib qoladi — artiklsiz: young people, Italian food, modern art, organic vegetables. the — faqat aniq, chegaralangan guruh uchun.

sentences.text: **Young people** today change jobs much more often than their parents did.
sentences.translation: Bugungi **yoshlar** ota-onalariga qaraganda ishni ancha tez-tez almashtiradi.

sentences.text: I don't really like **modern art** — I prefer old paintings.
sentences.translation: **Zamonaviy san'atni** unchalik yoqtirmayman — eski rasmlar ko'proq yoqadi.

sentences.text: **Italian food** is popular all over the world, but **Uzbek food** is catching up.
sentences.translation: **Italyan taomlari** butun dunyoda mashhur, lekin **o'zbek taomlari** ham ulardan qolishmayapti.

sentences.text: **Organic vegetables** are expensive, but many people think they're worth it.
sentences.translation: **Organik sabzavotlar** qimmat, lekin ko'pchilik ular bunga arziydi deb hisoblaydi.

sentences.text: **Small businesses** often struggle in their first two years.
sentences.translation: **Kichik bizneslar** ko'pincha dastlabki ikki yilda qiynaladi.

sentences.text: **The young people** in our street organised a clean-up of the park.
sentences.translation: Ko'chamizdagi **yoshlar** bog'ni tozalash tadbirini uyushtirishdi.

sentences.text: **Second-hand clothes** are much cheaper and better for the environment.
sentences.translation: **Ishlatilgan kiyimlar** ancha arzon va atrof-muhit uchun foydaliroq.

sentences.text: Sarah collects **old maps**, especially maps of Central Asia.
sentences.translation: Sara **eski xaritalar** yig'adi, ayniqsa Markaziy Osiyo xaritalarini.

sentences.text: **Fresh bread** smells wonderful, and **the fresh bread** from the bakery on our corner is the best in town.
sentences.translation: **Yangi non** ajoyib hid taratadi, burchakdagi novvoyxonaning **yangi noni** esa shahardagi eng zo'ri.

sentences.text: **Large cities** offer more opportunities, but **the large cities** I've lived in were all too noisy for me.
sentences.translation: **Katta shaharlar** ko'proq imkoniyat beradi, lekin men yashagan **katta shaharlarning** hammasi menga juda shovqinli tuyulgan.

examples.title: **people who** ... / **the people who** ...
examples.description: Aniqlovchi ergash gap ham o'z-o'zidan the keltirmaydi: people who smoke — umumiy toifa (kim chekmasin). the people who live next door — aniq odamlar.

sentences.text: **People who** exercise regularly usually sleep better.
sentences.translation: Muntazam sport bilan shug'ullanadigan **odamlar** odatda yaxshiroq uxlaydi.

sentences.text: **The people who** live next door have three noisy dogs.
sentences.translation: Qo'shni uyda yashaydigan **odamlarning** uchta shovqinli iti bor.

sentences.text: **Students who** work part-time often get lower marks.
sentences.translation: Yarim stavkada ishlaydigan **talabalar** ko'pincha pastroq baho oladi.

sentences.text: **The students who** failed the test can take it again on Friday.
sentences.translation: Testdan o'ta olmagan **talabalar** uni juma kuni qayta topshirishi mumkin.

sentences.text: I don't trust **people who** never admit their mistakes.
sentences.translation: Hech qachon xatosini tan olmaydigan **odamlarga** ishonmayman.

sentences.text: **Cars that** run on petrol will be banned in some cities.
sentences.translation: Ayrim shaharlarda benzinda yuradigan **mashinalar** taqiqlanadi.

sentences.text: **Shops that** sell local crafts attract a lot of tourists in Bukhara.
sentences.translation: Buxoroda mahalliy hunarmandchilik buyumlarini sotadigan **do'konlar** ko'p sayyohni jalb qiladi.

sentences.text: Bekzod thanked **the nurses who** had looked after him.
sentences.translation: Bekzod o'ziga qaragan **hamshiralarga** minnatdorchilik bildirdi.

sentences.text: Did you find **the documents that** I left on your desk?
sentences.translation: Stolingizga qoldirgan **hujjatlarimni** topdingizmi?

sentences.text: **Companies that** ignore customers' complaints don't survive long — **the company** I used to work for closed last year.
sentences.translation: Mijozlar shikoyatiga e'tibor bermaydigan **kompaniyalar** uzoq yashamaydi — men ishlagan **kompaniya** o'tgan yili yopildi.

examples.title: **Uzbek history** / **the history of** Uzbekistan
examples.description: Mavhum ot sifat bilan — artiklsiz (Uzbek history, modern society, international law); of bilan aniqlansa — the (the history of the Silk Road, the role of women).

sentences.text: Kate is writing a book about **Uzbek history** for British readers.
sentences.translation: Keyt britaniyalik o'quvchilar uchun **O'zbekiston tarixi** haqida kitob yozyapti.

sentences.text: **The history of** the Silk Road is full of surprising stories.
sentences.translation: **Ipak yo'li tarixi** ajoyib voqealarga to'la.

sentences.text: She's doing research on **the role of** women in medieval society.
sentences.translation: U o'rta asrlar jamiyatida **ayollarning roli** bo'yicha tadqiqot olib boryapti.

sentences.text: **Modern society** depends completely on electricity.
sentences.translation: **Zamonaviy jamiyat** butunlay elektr energiyasiga bog'liq.

sentences.text: Have you read anything about **the life of** Alisher Navoi?
sentences.translation: **Alisher Navoiyning hayoti** haqida biror narsa o'qiganmisiz?

sentences.text: **The education of** girls in rural areas has improved a lot.
sentences.translation: Qishloq joylarida **qizlarning ta'limi** ancha yaxshilandi.

sentences.text: Jasur is studying **international law** at a university in London.
sentences.translation: Jasur Londondagi bir universitetda **xalqaro huquqni** o'rganyapti.

sentences.text: **The quality of** life in small towns is often higher than people think.
sentences.translation: Kichik shaharchalarda **hayot sifati** ko'pincha odamlar o'ylaganidan yuqori.

sentences.text: Oliver is fascinated by **Islamic architecture**, especially the tilework of Samarkand.
sentences.translation: Oliver **islom me'morchiligiga**, ayniqsa Samarqand koshinkorligiga mahliyo.

sentences.text: **Environmental problems** affect everyone, but **the problems of** the Aral Sea region are especially serious.
sentences.translation: **Ekologik muammolar** hammaga ta'sir qiladi, lekin Orolbo'yi hududining **muammolari** ayniqsa jiddiy.

examples.title: **most people** / **most of the people**
examples.description: Umumiy ma'noda — most / all / some + ot (artiklsiz): Most people, All children. Aniq guruh ichida — most of the / all the / some of the.

sentences.text: **Most people** in Fergana grow fruit in their gardens, even in the city.
sentences.translation: Farg'onada, hatto shaharda ham, **ko'pchilik odamlar** hovlisida meva yetishtiradi.

sentences.text: **Most of the people** at the meeting agreed with the plan.
sentences.translation: Yig'ilishdagi **odamlarning ko'pchiligi** reja bilan rozi bo'ldi.

sentences.text: **All children** need love and attention, whatever their age.
sentences.translation: Yoshidan qat'i nazar, **barcha bolalarga** mehr va e'tibor kerak.

sentences.text: **All the children** in Dilnoza's class went on the trip to Khiva.
sentences.translation: Dilnozaning sinfidagi **barcha bolalar** Xivaga sayohatga borishdi.

sentences.text: **Some students** prefer online lessons because they can study at night.
sentences.translation: **Ayrim talabalar** onlayn darslarni afzal ko'radi, chunki kechasi o'qiy oladi.

sentences.text: **Some of the students** in my group have never been abroad.
sentences.translation: Guruhimdagi **talabalarning ba'zilari** hech qachon chet elda bo'lmagan.

sentences.text: **Most of the food** at the wedding was cooked by the bride's relatives.
sentences.translation: To'ydagi **taomlarning ko'p qismini** kelinning qarindoshlari pishirgan.

sentences.text: According to the report, **most food** in supermarkets contains too much sugar.
sentences.translation: Hisobotga ko'ra, supermarketlardagi **oziq-ovqatning ko'pi** haddan tashqari shakarli.

sentences.text: Not **all teenagers** are addicted to their phones — my son hardly uses his.
sentences.translation: **Hamma o'smirlar** ham telefonga mukkasidan ketgan emas — o'g'lim telefonini deyarli ishlatmaydi.

sentences.text: Although **most tourists** visit only Samarkand and Bukhara, **most of the ones** we met preferred Khiva.
sentences.translation: **Sayyohlarning ko'pchiligi** faqat Samarqand va Buxoroni ko'rsa ham, biz uchratganlarning **aksariyati** Xivani afzal ko'rdi.

examples.title: Mixed: general and specific in one sentence
examples.description: Aralash mustahkamlash: bir gapning o'zida umumiy (artiklsiz) va aniq (the) ma'no — murakkabroq gaplarda.

sentences.text: **Dogs** are usually friendly, but **the dog** next door barks at everyone.
sentences.translation: **Itlar** odatda do'stona bo'ladi, lekin qo'shnining **iti** hammaga vovullaydi.

sentences.text: I rarely drink **coffee**, but I couldn't refuse **the coffee** Kate made with cardamom.
sentences.translation: Men **qahvani** kam ichaman, lekin Keyt kardamon bilan damlagan **qahvani** rad eta olmadim.

sentences.text: **Life** isn't always fair, and **the life** of a refugee shows that very clearly.
sentences.translation: **Hayot** doim ham adolatli emas, **qochqinning hayoti** buni juda aniq ko'rsatadi.

sentences.text: **Tourists** love Khiva at night, when **the streets** of the old city are quiet.
sentences.translation: **Sayyohlar** Xivani kechasi, eski shahar **ko'chalari** jimjit bo'lganda yaxshi ko'radi.

sentences.text: **Water** is precious in the desert, so **the water** in this well is never wasted.
sentences.translation: Cho'lda **suv** qimmatli, shuning uchun bu quduqdagi **suv** hech qachon isrof qilinmaydi.

sentences.text: Aziz has always loved **nature**, so he spent his holiday walking in **the mountains**.
sentences.translation: Aziz doim **tabiatni** yaxshi ko'rgan, shuning uchun ta'tilini **tog'larda** sayr qilib o'tkazdi.

sentences.text: What do you think about **social media**? — I use it, but **the comments** under my posts annoy me.
sentences.translation: **Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar** haqida nima deysiz? — Ishlataman, lekin postlarim ostidagi **izohlar** asabimga tegadi.

sentences.text: **Books** are expensive these days, so Emma borrows **the books** she needs from the library.
sentences.translation: Hozir **kitoblar** qimmat, shuning uchun Emma kerakli **kitoblarni** kutubxonadan olib turadi.

sentences.text: In my opinion, **good teachers** matter more than **the buildings** they teach in.
sentences.translation: Menimcha, **yaxshi o'qituvchilar** ular dars beradigan **binolardan** muhimroq.

sentences.text: **Crime** is rare in our neighbourhood, so **the robbery** at the corner shop last week shocked everyone.
sentences.translation: Mahallamizda **jinoyat** kam uchraydi, shuning uchun o'tgan hafta burchakdagi do'konda bo'lgan **o'g'irlik** hammani larzaga soldi.
